title: Package GPIO Control Panel as Linux-runnable app bundle

requirements.text: Configure the Vite build to use a relative base path (`./`) so that all asset references in the built static bundle work correctly when served from any directory on a local Linux Apache or file server.

quotes: make this into an app that runs on Linux

acceptanceCriteria: Running `npm run build` produces a `dist/` folder where all JS, CSS, and asset URLs are relative (start with `./`).
The built `index.html` loads correctly when opened from a local Apache server at any virtual host path.
No absolute `/assets/` paths appear in the compiled output.

requirements.text: Update the GPIO HTTP endpoint in `gpioHttp.ts` to use plain `http://localhost:3000` (not HTTPS) so that the frontend can reach the local GPIO server when deployed on Linux without TLS configuration.

quotes: make this into an app that runs on Linux

acceptanceCriteria: HTTP POST requests to the GPIO server use `http://localhost:3000` as the base URL.
No mixed-content or HTTPS errors appear in the browser console when sending GPIO signals from a locally served page.
The DebugHttpPanel successfully fires test requests to `http://localhost:3000` when a GPIO server is running.

requirements.text: Update the `linux_bundle_run.sh` and `package_linux_bundle.sh` scripts to include all necessary deployment artifacts (built frontend `dist/`, backend canister WASM, `dfx.json`, Apache vhost config example, and the `rpi_event_runner.sh` script) in a single timestamped `.tar.gz` bundle that a user can extract and run on a fresh Linux machine with `dfx` and Apache installed.

quotes: make this into an app that runs on Linux

acceptanceCriteria: Running `./scripts/package_linux_bundle.sh` produces a `.tar.gz` file containing the frontend `dist/`, backend canister artifacts, and all helper scripts.
The bundle includes a top-level `README.md` or `INSTALL.md` with step-by-step Linux setup instructions.
Extracting and following the included instructions on a Linux machine with `dfx` and Apache results in a working control panel accessible via browser.

requirements.text: Create or update a Linux installation guide (`frontend/docs/linux-local-test-bundle.md`) that covers: prerequisites (Node.js, dfx, Apache), building the bundle, deploying the local ICP replica, configuring Apache to serve the `dist/` folder, starting the GPIO server on port 3000, and verifying the full stack is operational.

quotes: make this into an app that runs on Linux

acceptanceCriteria: The document lists all prerequisites with recommended versions.
Step-by-step instructions are present for Apache vhost setup, dfx replica startup, and frontend serving.
A troubleshooting section addresses common issues (CORS, mixed content, port conflicts).

constraints: All Motoko backend logic must remain in the single-actor `backend/main.mo` file.
Do not modify any files under `frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts`, `frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts`, `frontend/src/main.tsx`, or `frontend/src/components/ui`.
Do not introduce external databases, cloud services, or non-ICP backend dependencies.
nonGoals: Windows or macOS packaging — Linux only.
Remote/cloud deployment; this is strictly for local Linux execution.
Changes to the GPIO pin mapping or backend canister data model.
